definition: A word embedding is a numerical vector that places a word in a space where distances or directions can reflect learned patterns in its usage.
example: A search system uses nearby vectors to find terms used in similar contexts.

definition: Word processing is the creation, editing and formatting of text documents using software.
example: An author applies heading styles and reviews tracked edits before exporting a report.

definition: Word VBA uses Visual Basic for Applications within Microsoft Word to automate tasks and control document objects.
example: An editor runs a macro that applies consistent formatting to recurring headings.

definition: word2vec is a set of neural methods for learning word vectors by predicting words or their contexts from a corpus.
example: An analyst trains word vectors on customer reviews to compare words used in similar contexts.

definition: Workers’ compensation claims are requests for benefits under a program covering qualifying work-related injury or illness.
example: A claims specialist documents an accident report and reviews the supporting records.
sense_note: Eligibility and procedures vary by jurisdiction.

definition: Workflow automation uses software to carry out predefined steps or transitions with reduced manual intervention.
example: A completed form automatically routes to the appropriate reviewer.

definition: Workflow management designs, coordinates and monitors how work moves among people and systems.
example: A manager tracks which approval step is delaying new requests.

definition: Workforce optimisation uses staffing data and practices to align schedules, skills and deployment with service demand and other constraints.
example: A contact center adjusts shift coverage to match predicted peak call times.

definition: Working with children aged 0–5 involves providing developmentally appropriate care and learning support for infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
example: A caregiver adapts a group activity so toddlers can participate safely and independently.

definition: Writing outlines organizes a proposed text into main points, supporting details and a logical sequence.
example: A writer groups evidence under three section headings before drafting an essay.

definition: WSDL2Java refers to tools that generate Java code or bindings from a Web Services Description Language document.
example: A developer generates client bindings for an existing SOAP service.
sense_note: The label can refer to similarly named commands from different toolkits, including Apache Axis and Apache CXF.

definition: wxGTK is the wxWidgets implementation for systems using the GTK graphical toolkit.
example: A developer builds a wxWidgets desktop application with the GTK backend on Linux.

definition: wxPerl provides Perl bindings for building graphical applications with wxWidgets.
example: A maintainer updates the controls in a legacy Perl desktop application.

definition: wxPython provides Python bindings for the wxWidgets graphical user interface toolkit.
example: A developer creates a desktop form with native-looking menus and buttons.

definition: Wyse Management Suite centrally configures and manages supported Dell endpoints such as thin clients.
example: An administrator assigns a common configuration profile to a group of thin clients.

definition: The xanthoproteic reaction is a qualitative color reaction that indicates the presence of certain aromatic amino acid residues in a sample.
example: A chemistry class relates the observed qualitative color change to aromatic groups in proteins.

definition: Xbox Live Vision was a camera accessory for the Xbox 360 that supported compatible games and video features.
example: A player uses the camera for video chat in a supported legacy Xbox experience.

definition: Xcalibur is Thermo Scientific software for acquiring and processing data from compatible mass spectrometry instruments.
example: An analyst reviews a recorded chromatogram and its associated mass spectra.

definition: XtraGrid is a DevExpress grid control for displaying and editing structured data in Windows Forms applications.
example: A developer adds column filtering to an order table.
sense_note: The older XtraGrid name is associated with the DevExpress WinForms Data Grid.

definition: Yahoo Messenger was an instant messaging service that supported conversations and presence information.
example: A user could see whether a contact was online before starting a chat.

definition: YARA describes and matches patterns in files or data for tasks such as identifying known types of suspicious content.
example: A security analyst checks files gathered in an authorized investigation against reviewed detection rules.

definition: Yardi provides software for managing real estate operations, accounting and property records.
example: A property manager uses a Yardi application to reconcile occupancy and rent records.
sense_note: The label is a vendor and product family, not one specific application.

definition: Yellow Dog Linux was a Linux distribution developed for systems including PowerPC hardware.
example: An archivist boots a compatible older machine to inspect an application built on Yellow Dog Linux.

definition: Youth mentoring is a supportive relationship in which a mentor helps a young person build skills, confidence and direction over time.
example: A mentor helps a teen plan and reflect on a first community project.

definition: YunOS was an operating system developed by Alibaba for connected devices including smartphones.
example: A mobile software archivist identifies a device that originally ran YunOS.
sense_note: Names and product branding changed over time.

definition: z/OS is IBM’s operating system for mainframes, designed to support enterprise workloads such as transactions and batch processing.
example: An operator checks the results of an overnight batch job on a z/OS system.

definition: Z-Wave is a low-power wireless communications technology used to connect compatible automation devices.
example: A home automation controller receives status updates from a compatible door sensor.

definition: Zemax OpticStudio is software for designing and analyzing optical systems through modeling and ray tracing.
example: An engineer compares lens designs to reduce image distortion.

definition: ZENworks Asset Management inventories hardware and software and supports tracking software licenses and usage.
example: An IT team compares installed applications with its license entitlements.

definition: zeroheight is a platform for publishing and maintaining design-system documentation.
example: A design systems team documents when to use a particular button component.

definition: Zerto provides replication and orchestration tools for recovering workloads after disruptions or moving them between environments.
example: An infrastructure team tests whether a replicated workload can be recovered in a designated environment.

definition: Zetafax is a software platform for sending, receiving and managing faxes through a networked service.
example: An office routes incoming faxes to an internal inbox.

definition: ZFS integrates a filesystem and volume management, with features such as data checksums, snapshots and pooled storage.
example: An administrator takes a read-only snapshot so a prior file version can be recovered.
